# FUTURE ME CAME BACK

[Intro — distant piano, tape hiss]

**PRESENT:**
Three in the morning, ceiling turning into space,
Breathing slow and steady, letting stillness set the pace.
I keep asking tomorrow what it wants me to become—
Then somebody knocked three times,
and I knew my answer had come.

[Verse 1 — Present Me]

Door cracked open, there I stood, but older in the eyes,
Same spark, same soul, just calmer, clearer, more alive.
I said, “Who the hell are you?”
He said, “You already know.
I’ve only got three minutes—
there are things you need to know.”

I said, “Do we make it?
Do the pieces come in place?
Do I learn to trust the process
without needing every answer traced?

Do the dreams inside my mind
become something I can see?”

He smiled like he'd been waiting years:

**FUTURE:**
“You have no idea what happens to me.”

[Pre-Chorus]

**PRESENT:**
Tell me the ending.

**FUTURE:**
No.

**PRESENT:**
Tell me the way.

**FUTURE:**
Better than that—
you learn to choose today.

[Chorus]

**FUTURE:**
Keep moving with faith,
you have no idea how much works out.
Thoughts are just thoughts,
you can question the story
and choose what you believe about now.

Breathe into the moment,
put both feet down,
let the present become solid ground.
You don't need every answer
to take one good step
toward the life you're building now.

You don't need the map.
You don't need to know how.

Stay present.
Choose wisely.
Keep becoming now.

'Cause you have no idea—
no idea—
how much works out.

[Verse 2 — Present Me]

**PRESENT:**
“Do I find love?”

**FUTURE:**
“Yes—when you learn to receive.”

**PRESENT:**
“Do I find purpose?”

**FUTURE:**
“More than you currently believe.”

**PRESENT:**
“Do I understand myself?”

**FUTURE:**
“More deeply every year.”

**PRESENT:**
“What changes everything?”

**FUTURE:**
“You learn you can choose your response with clarity.”

A thought isn't a prophecy.
A feeling isn't fate.
You notice what's arising,
then decide what you create.

Name what you're feeling.
Breathe before reacting.
Let your values choose the next move
instead of simply acting.

You learn to hold two truths at once:
“I accept where I am today,
and I can still keep growing
in a beautiful new way.”

You stop demanding certainty
before you take a chance.
You let your wiser mind
put intention into action.

[Chorus]

**FUTURE:**
Keep moving with faith,
you have no idea how much works out.
People you haven't even met yet
will one day know what you're about.

Songs you haven't written,
rooms you haven't entered,
sunrises you've never seen—

There's a whole bright life
already unfolding
beyond what you currently believe.

You don't need the map.
You don't need to know how.

Stay present.
Choose wisely.
Keep becoming now.

You have no idea—
no idea—
how much works out.

[Bridge — music nearly disappears]

**PRESENT:**
Wait.

Before you go—

What's the one thing
you came all this way to tell me?

[Silence]

**FUTURE:**
I came back
to remind you you're becoming.

I came back
because your choices compound.

Every time you pause, breathe,
check the facts,
and put both feet on the ground—

you change your direction.

Every time you choose patience
instead of impulse—

you strengthen your future.

Every time you speak to yourself
like someone worth guiding—

you become your own teacher.

I remember this room.

I remember tonight.

I remember the exact moment
you realized:

Your mind can suggest a thought
without making that thought right.

You can observe it.

Question it.

Reframe it.

Choose again.

And that tiny space
between feeling and action?

That's where your future begins.

[Build]

**FUTURE:**
So if I could put one sentence
inside your bones forever—

It would be:

You don't have to control the whole sky
to learn to enjoy the weather.

[Final Chorus — full choir, orchestra, 808s]

KEEP MOVING WITH FAITH—
YOU HAVE NO IDEA HOW MUCH WORKS OUT!

The road gets wider,
the heart gets lighter,
your wiser mind keeps showing you how.

There are hands you'll hold,
stories untold,
whole cities beneath your feet.

There are versions of you
you would barely believe
if tonight was all you could see.

So breathe.

Check the facts.

Choose what matters.

Come back to now.

Build one beautiful decision
on another somehow.

Stay present.
Stay grateful.
Let your values lead you out.

Someday you'll look backward
and wish you could tell yourself now:

You have no idea—
no idea—
no idea how much works out.

[Outro — future voice fading]

**PRESENT:**
Will I ever see you again?

**FUTURE:**
Every morning.

Every good choice.

Every time you choose
the life you're becoming.

# THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED

**[Intro]**
I wore the weight of a wall that was smoke,
Called it a cage, never questioned the joke.
Hands on the bars, heart hard in the dark,
Till I pushed once lightly—
and everything sparked.

**[Verse 1]**
I counted my losses like locks on a door,
Fed every fear till it begged me for more.
Doubt did the talking, I treated it true,
Built me a border nobody else drew.

I made every maybe a mountain of stone,
Made every silence mean I was alone.
Mind made a movie, then called it a fact,
But thoughts are just thoughts—I can question the act.

Pressure made diamonds, but patience made plans,
Pain made me panic, then purpose made hands.
I stopped asking shadows which road I should take,
Put truth to the test and discovered the fake.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
All of that running, all of that strain,
All of those stories rehearsing the pain—
I reached for the handle expecting a fight...

It opened.

**[Chorus]**
**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
I was waiting for a key.
Had the whole wide world ahead,
Had the warden inside me.

**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
All that thunder, all that talk—
Fear can paint a prison,
But it cannot stop the walk.

Push once.
Step through.
See what the light does.
I thought freedom had to find me—
**I just had to rise up.**

**[Verse 2]**
Now I don't bow to the first thing I feel,
Feeling is weather—it isn't the wheel.
Storm in my skull? Let it thunder, then pass.
I steer by the compass, not clouds in the glass.

Wise mind, wide eyes, both feet on the ground,
Breathe through the noise till the signal gets found.
Facts over fiction, intention over fear,
One clean decision can change a whole year.

I used to need certainty carved into gold,
Now I move carefully even when cold.
Courage ain't knowing the ending beforehand—
Courage is moving with doubt in your hand.

And winning ain't proving the doubters were wrong,
Winning is learning you belonged all along.
Winning is opening doors as you climb,
Then holding them open for somebody behind.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
So if there's a wall where your daylight should be,
Don't worship the wall—check what you can see.
Don't bleed on a barrier built out of thought...

**Try the lock.**

**[Chorus]**
**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
I was waiting for a key.
Had the whole wide world ahead,
Had the warden inside me.

**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
All that thunder, all that talk—
Fear can paint a prison,
But it cannot stop the walk.

Push once.
Step through.
See what the light does.
I thought freedom had to find me—
**I just had to rise up.**

**[Bridge — piano drops almost alone]**
Maybe the mountain is massive.
Maybe the road really hurts.
Maybe some chains are actual chains,
And breaking them takes real work.

But never let fear forge another
And fasten it onto your name.
Separate fact from the prophecy—
Then walk through whatever remains.

One breath.
One truth.
One deliberate move.
No prophecy needed—
Just something to prove.

Not to them.

**To you.**

**[Final Chorus — huge choir]**
**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
Hear the hinges when they swing.
Every step beyond the boundary
Makes another spirit sing.

**THE GATES WERE NEVER LOCKED.**
Let the old illusion fall.
Freedom isn't feeling fearless—
**Freedom's moving through it all.**

Push once.
Break through.
Bring everybody up.
Turn the keys into a kingdom,
Turn the scars into enough.

No cage.
No crown
Can tell me where I stop.

I finally touched the doorway—

**THE GATES
WERE
NEVER
LOCKED.**

# Rich Before the Money

**[Intro]**
Before the bands, before the brand,
before the bright lights knew my name—
I had breath inside my body,
I had blood inside my veins.
Turns out I had plenty.

**[Verse 1]**
Sun spilling gold through a slit in the shade,
steam from the coffee, another day made,
feet on the floor and a roof overhead,
food in the fridge and a dream in my head.

Phone full of people who pick up at two,
friends know my flaws and still follow me through,
family calling just checking I’m straight—
fortune was hiding in plain sight all day.

Chasing the chain, chasing change, chasing cheers,
measuring miracles yearly in tiers,
while the wind through the window kept whispering clear:
“You got somebody who loves you—your treasure is here.”

Stars for a ceiling, songs for the stress,
scars saying somehow I survived every mess,
heart that could hurt, heal, hope and progress—
I was begging for more while already blessed.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
Counted every dollar that I didn’t possess,
never counted every “call me if you’re stressed.”
Counted every door that slammed in my face,
never counted every morning arriving with grace.

**[Chorus]**
I was **rich before the money,**
rich before the racks,
rich when all I had was hope
and a little gas in the tank.

Rich with the rain running,
rich with the sun above me,
rich with a table
and somebody who loved me.

**Rich before the money.**
Before the gold, before the glory,
before the whole world heard my story—
I had love, I had life,
I had more than enough for me.
I was **rich before the money.**

**[Verse 2]**
Clean cold water—what’s richer than that?
Laugh so hard that you lean all the way back.
Dog by the doorway, dusk going dark,
moon on the windshield and miles in the heart.

Fresh pair of socks and a song hitting right,
safe trip home through the soft city lights,
somebody texting me, “Tell me you’re fine,”
all of these diamonds that never get mined.

We want bigger, brighter, better, more—
more square feet, more seats, more keys, more doors,
but a mansion means nothing when peace packs its bags,
and a million means little when love never lasts.

Give me good people and give me good purpose,
give me the grit when the work feels worthless,
give me the wisdom to notice what’s working—
wealth isn’t wealth if your spirit stays starving.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
Count every kindness, count every call,
count every hand that reached when you’d fall.
Count every breath you were never guaranteed—
suddenly enough starts looking like everything.

**[Bridge]**
If all the glitter disappeared tonight,
leave me love, leave me light.
Leave me laughter round a kitchen table,
leave me strength enough to know I’m able.

Leave me stars when the streetlights fade,
leave me peace that a price can’t pay.
Fortunes fall and fortunes flee,
but what is priceless stays with me.

**[Rap Build]**
Big bank someday—beautiful, bring it,
but I won’t let a balance determine my spirit.
Build big buildings, buy brilliant things,
still know breakfast with family can feel like a kingdom.

Bread breaking, belly laughing, breeze in the trees,
bare feet, back porch, being at peace.
Blessed with a breath and the freedom to breathe—
what billionaire buys one more heartbeat guaranteed?

No receipt for relief.
No price tag on peace.
No market for memories.
No lease on belief.

When success comes dressed in diamonds and drums,
I’ll remember exactly where all of this begun:
not a vault, not a yacht, not applause from a crowd—
just being alive and awake enough to notice it now.

**[Final Chorus]**
I was **RICH BEFORE THE MONEY,**
rich before the fame,
rich when nobody knew me,
still had love beside my name.

Rich with the rain running,
rich with the sun above me,
rich with these scars, these stars,
these arms around me.

**RICH BEFORE THE MONEY,**
before the gold, before the glory,
before the whole world heard my story.
I had breath, I had love,
I had life pouring through me.

And if the millions come tomorrow,
I’ll thank God—but they won’t define me.

**Rich before the money.
Rich before the money.**

Turns out—
**I had plenty.**

# Victory With Nobody Dead

**[Intro – piano, distant choir]**
What if the bravest battle
was the one we never had?
What if the greatest victory
sent every soldier back?

**[Verse 1 – rap]**
They said pick a side, I said pick up the pieces,
Peace got a price, but revenge never ceases.
Preachers preach peace while the presidents posture,
Families fracture while the cameras capture.
Maps get marked by a man in a room,
Then a mother gets flowers where a son used to bloom.
Medals on a mantle, names carved in granite,
Everybody screaming they’re defending the planet.

But tell me who won when the playground burned?
Who gained ground when the children never returned?
Who conquered what when the hospitals fell?
If victory looks like this, victory looks like hell.

**[Pre-Chorus – female vocal]**
Bring them home, bring them home,
Let the babies grow old.
Let the stories get written
without names carved in stone.

**[Chorus – massive duet]**
**I want a win where nobody dies,**
No smoke in the sun, no fire in the skies.
No mother on the phone asking heaven why,
No folded-up flag where her child should lie.

**Give me a victory with nobody dead,**
Bread on the table, not bloodshed instead.
Hands held high but no guns overhead—
**That’s my kind of victory: nobody dead.**

**[Verse 2 – rap]**
Real strength ain’t rage, real power is patience,
Talk through the tension, transform the nations.
Courage is calling when hatred says hide,
Finding some humanity over the divide.

The enemy eats, the enemy sleeps,
The enemy laughs and the enemy weeps.
The enemy’s daughter draws stars on a page,
The enemy’s father gets scared and gets aged.

Same little heartbeat, same oxygen breath,
Same desperate instinct to bargain with death.
Different translation, identical prayer:
“Please bring my family home from out there.”

So cancel the countdown, cut through the pride,
Put diplomats deep where the missiles would ride.
If somebody tells me compassion is weak,
I’ll tell ’em restraint takes the strength of the meek.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
Bring them home, bring them home,
Every daughter, every son.
The greatest war we’ll ever win
is the war that never comes.

**[Chorus]**
**I want a win where nobody dies,**
No smoke in the sun, no fire in the skies.
No mother on the phone asking heaven why,
No folded-up flag where her child should lie.

**Give me a victory with nobody dead,**
Bread on the table, not bloodshed instead.
Hands held high but no guns overhead—
**That’s my kind of victory: nobody dead.**

**[Bridge – stripped piano / female lead]**
What if mercy made the headlines?
What if treaties topped the charts?
What if leaders measured greatness
by the number of beating hearts?

No revenge passed down like inheritance,
No child taught an ancient arrogance.
Let tomorrow wake without yesterday’s debt—
Forgive what we can.
Prevent what comes next.

**[Final Rap – drums build]**
Let the tanks turn tractors, let the trenches grow trees,
Let the factories manufacture medicine and peace.
Let the pilots fly people safely back home,
Let the drones shoot movies, let the battlefields grow.

Spend the billions on bridges, on bedrooms, on bread,
On keeping people living instead of counting the dead.
Call me naïve—I’d rather be that
Than clever enough to make a cemetery map.

We’ve mastered destruction, now master restraint,
Make peace look powerful, make mercy look great.
The hardest flex left on this planet instead
Is winning the whole thing—

**with nobody dead.**

**[Final Chorus – huge choir + rap ad-libs]**
**I want a win where nobody dies,**
No smoke in the sun, no fire in the skies.
Every mother gets her child back alive,
Every enemy becomes somebody we survived **with**.

**Give me a victory with nobody dead,**
Hope in the heart and a roof overhead.
Stars still shining when the history gets read—
**That’s my kind of victory: nobody dead.**

Nobody dead.
Everybody fed.
Nobody dead.
Let tomorrow live instead.

**Nobody dead.**

I don’t hand it my mouth just because it feels right.

What hurt me doesn’t have to hurt through me,
what burned me doesn’t get to become what I breathe.
I can break the chain without breaking a soul—
turn the pain into purpose, turn the pressure into gold.

**[Chorus]**
**Become the person you needed,**
give the love you were pleading for.
Hold the door, hold your word,
hold a heart when it hits the floor.

**Become the person you needed,**
be the proof that the cycle can cease.
Leave more light than you borrowed,
leave more love, leave more peace.

**[Bridge — Piano Drops Bare]**
Listen first.
Speak with care.
Tell the truth.
Always share.

Protect the small.
Forgive, but learn.
Give what you can.
Let kindness return.

Build, don’t break.
Bless, don’t boast.
Love the lonely.
Feed the hope.

make one corner kinder.

**[Final Chorus — Huge]**

make your history useful somehow.

but you’re writing tomorrow right now.

**Become the person you needed,**
let your character speak when you leave.

but who stood taller because you believed.

If you needed somebody—**be somebody.**
If you needed some mercy—**give.**
Leave more light than you borrowed—
that’s a beautiful reason to live.

**[Outro]**
One better choice.
One kinder deed.
One promise kept.
One person freed.

I stopped asking the world
for everything I didn’t receive.

Now I’m becoming
the person
I needed
to meet.
